title: How often does anyone say no?
question: Of the money files that reached a final vote at the Board of Supervisors each year, what share passed without a single no vote?
finding: From 2015 to 9 November 2026 the Board cast a recorded final vote on 3,483 contracts, leases, grants, settlements and appropriations. 3,359 (96.4%) passed without a single no vote, 2,703 of them with every listed member voting aye. 121 passed over at least one no and 3 were voted down. By year the share passed with no dissent runs from 92.6% (2016) to 99.7% (2019), with no steady rise or fall. The 124 files with a no vote were decided on 82 separate vote lists: 47 of them are one member’s no repeated down 9 same-day lists of 3 or more files.
how: A money file is a Board file that approves a contract, lease, grant agreement, loan, settlement with a business, accepted grant, emergency contract or appropriation (3,907 files introduced since 2014). Its final vote is the last roll call at the full Board on the measure itself (adopted, approved, passed on first reading or finally passed), which is the definition shared with the other pages that use these roll calls. “Passed with no dissent” means the result is Pass and no member is printed as voting No; members printed as excused or absent do not count either way. The year is the year of that vote. A vote list is one day’s identical line-up of ayes and noes. 6 ordinances are counted on their first-reading vote because no later roll call is recorded for them. Other pages count 123 of these votes as divided, meaning both ayes and noes; the count here is one higher wherever a file was voted down with no aye at all (1).
limits: A unanimous vote is the ordinary result and no sign of anything wrong. 3,419 of the 3,483 files were recommended by a committee before the Board voted, 900 accept a grant or gift, and 1,104 amend or extend an agreement already in place. Of the 770 files of $10 million or more introduced since 2019, 650 carry a report by the Board’s Budget and Legislative Analyst among their attachments, so a vote with no dissent can follow written scrutiny at the committee stage. A no vote is ordinary; the vote pages give no reasons, and dissent can reflect a disagreement about policy or the budget rather than doubt about the organization named in the file. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. 423 more money files have no recorded Board vote at all: their votes were before 2015, or they were filed, tabled or are still pending. “Excused” is printed for a member who was out of the room or away as well as for one excused from voting; the page does not say which, and it is never read here as anything else. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
